title: Value of Dose-Rounding Policies over a Growing Grid of Prescription Midpoints
banked_reason: D0.5: graded subfield below field floor; score ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The causal interpretation, however, is conditional on the explicit pointwise structural-trace restriction, so the result does not identify atomic policy values from exchangeability and observed-law smoothness alone.

The contribution remains tied to a fixed finite-stratum, known regular midpoint grid with Hölder-one regression and supplies no data application or numerical study demonstrating the practical magnitude of the transition.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived a matched n^(-1/2)+(nm)^(-1/3) minimax risk and honest-length frontier, an observable estimator and interval, a same-class converse, and distinct direct-risk and Wald-inference transitions. Citation and mathematical checks passed after the Lindeberg-Feller source was attested and its locator corrected. D0.5 capped the sound result at subfield for the stated scope and evidence limits; the field-floor run stopped before Lean formalization.
tldr: Rounding a continuous dose to \(m\) prescription midpoints creates a growing atomic policy whose value is a weighted average of \(m\) regression traces with unknown bin weights. The project derives the uniform frontier \(n^{-1/2}+(nm)^{-1/3}\) for both minimax absolute risk and \(90\%\)-honest expected interval length. A split-sample aggregate local-mean estimator handles coarse grids without a density estimator or a \(\log m\) penalty, direct reward averaging handles fine grids, coherent bumps at every midpoint give the same-class converse, and separate theorems distinguish the \(m\asymp\sqrt n\) risk elbow from the stricter Wald-validity condition \(m/\sqrt n\to\infty\).
gap: Continuous-policy kernel estimators treat a covariate-indexed dose, modified-policy influence-function theory requires regular transformations, and the closest accepted minimax result controls one atom. None of the inspected results gives matched risk and honest expected length for a growing set of rounding atoms under an unknown merely measurable treatment density.
fill: Conditioning on split-sample bin weights turns the fitting error into one disjoint-window weighted residual sum; a realized empty-window allowance yields honest coverage, while a coherent bump at every midpoint and a global shift match both terms of the derived frontier.
